$comment: PATTERN STUDY RESULTS — measured 2026-08-14 against the design of the same date.
10 queries, owner's profiled Chrome, >=18s apart, no block encountered.
HEADLINE: the hypothesis was half right, and the half that failed is the more
useful half. Query shape predicted the click-through rate exactly as written down
beforehand — all four CTR predictions held. But the AI Overview is NOT the
mechanism. Pattern D (exact calendar date, no city) carries NO AI Overview on
either sample and still earns 0 clicks on 126 impressions. Absence of an overview
is not sufficient for a click.
WHAT ACTUALLY SEPARATES: whether the query asks for a single data point. Asking
for one clock time (A, B, C, D, E) yields 3 clicks on 1738 impressions whatever
the SERP looks like. Asking for a direction (F) or a table across a month (G)
yields 2 clicks on 38. A point answer is satisfied by the overview, by a rival's
snippet, or by what the searcher already half-knows — no page needs opening.
STATISTICS, stated so the weakness is visible:
with-AIO 3/1612 = 0.19% vs without-AIO 2/164 = 1.22%, ratio 6.6x, Fisher
p = 0.070. NOT significant, and pattern D sits inside the without-AIO group
contributing 0/126. Regrouping as shape-not-time (F+G) 2/38 = 5.3% against
everything else 3/1609, Fisher p = 0.005 — but that regrouping was chosen AFTER
seeing the data, so the p-value is optimistic and should not be quoted as if it
were pre-registered. What IS pre-registered, and did hold, is the direction: F
and G were written down as the click-earning patterns before any query ran.
Underlying counts are tiny: F is 11 impressions and 1 click, G is 27 and 1.
SECOND FINDING, not designed for and with a caveat attached: we were absent from
the first page in 9 of 10 SERPs, while Search Console reports average positions
of 5.7 to 9.1 for the same queries. The one query where we did appear
(p-c-wien-sep, 5th organic at 1693px) is also one of the five queries in the whole
28-day report that earned a click. CAVEAT: a single reading per query cannot
distinguish 'we rank worse than GSC says' from ordinary day-to-day and
location-to-location variance — the 08-10 baseline saw us present one day and
gone the next on the same query. Treat as a thing to watch, not a measurement.
THIRD FINDING: alpenglowapp.com is cited inside the overview on 2 of the 6
overviews here (p-c-paris-sep, p-e-amanece-sep), consistent with the baseline.
It remains the closest comparable that gets cited where we do not.
METHOD LIMITATIONS of this run, recorded so no row is over-read:
- aioBottomPx comes from growing the label's ancestors until taller than 150px.
It can overshoot: in p-b-amsterdam-aug the first organic (908px) reads as
above the block bottom (981px). Bounds are indicative, not exact.
- aioCitedDomains is empty for p-a-roma-sep because the source box was
collapsed. Not expanded on purpose: fewer interactions, less block risk.
- Viewport was 932px (desktop extension window). Most of this traffic is
probably mobile, where usable height is nearer 660px and every 'first organic'
figure below would sit lower relative to the fold.
- No screenshots kept. Snippets and geometry are recorded instead; rows can be
re-measured but not re-audited pixel by pixel.
- present:false means absent from the loaded first page, not absent from the
index.
